newsitem.title: INDIA: India proposes tax on distributed profits of firms.
newsitem.headline: India proposes tax on distributed profits of firms.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday said he would abolish an unpopular tax on income from dividends, but at the same time proposed a 10 percent tax on the distributed profits of companies.
"Some companies distribute exorbitant dividends," Chidambaram told parliament while presenting the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
"Ideally, they should retain the bulk of their profits and plough them into fresh investments. I intend to reward companies who invest in future growth," the finance minister said.

"Hence I propose to levy a tax on distributed profits at the moderate rate of 10 percent on the amount so distributed," he said, adding that the tax would be imposed on firms and not passed on to shareholders.
Chidambaram said earlier in his budget speech that he planned to abolish a tax on dividend incomes. The government taxes shareholders on dividends, which are paid out of taxed profits.
